idiom_name: Express route handler per page (app.get('/orders', handler))
implementation_notes: Express turns the page into a route: app.get('/orders', handler) or a Router binds one handler function per method and path, the handler owns request handling and the domain calls, and res.render('orders', model) selects the view. The classic controller class is unnecessary - the callback is the controller - and shared behaviour is installed once as middleware ahead of the routes (app.use), which is Express' built-in answer to the duplication that page controllers invite. A bare node:http server with a hand-written path switch is the manual fallback when no framework is wanted.
pitfalls: Route order matters: the first matching route wins, so a broad path registered before a specific page silently shadows it.
Request-scoped state must stay on req/res (or res.locals): module-level variables are shared by every concurrent request.
In Express 4 a rejected promise inside an async handler does not reach the error middleware unless it is caught and passed to next(err).
